9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium wide, eye level, Scarlett (Image 2) bursts into the hallway with her coat over one arm and the lipstick in hand as the elevator doors begin closing, The narrow hallway leads into the elevator, with Scarlett (Image 2) entering on the left and the closing doors framing the Tired florist (Image 3), Courier (Image 4), and mirrored interior, INT. DOWNTOWN APARTMENT HALLWAY AND ELEVATOR — MORNING, morning, downtown_apartment_hallway_and_elevator (Image 5), Morning sunlight cuts into the elevator in moving bands as it drops through the building, creating shifting highlights across the mirrored walls and faces., Polished silver, cool gray, black wool, muted commuter clothing, green foliage, and bright coral., Scarlett (Image 2), tired_florist, Courier (Image 4), Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
Image 1 (primary): Primary source scene — generate 9 variant shots from this image
